deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the folio's study of systems of homogeneous linear congruences mod 1 with rational coefficients and integer unknowns. In modern terms: describe the lattice of integer vectors x with A·x in Z^m. Notation: [α, β, ...] is the positive generator of the Z-module spanned by rationals α, β, ... (their 'greatest common divisor'). Σ[α_r] + [1] is the module sum. 'mod 1/a' means 'lies in (1/a)Z'. The page is numbered 36. The faint Kurrent script underneath is an unrelated legal text (Entscheidung, Klägerin, Wolff ...), so Dedekind reused the paper.

(A) Top block: elimination step for the conditions left over from the previous page.
- The conditions are Σ e'κ'/p'' ≡ 0, Σ e'q'/p'' ≡ 0 and e' ≡ 0 (mod 1), in unknown integers e_1', e_2', ...
- Put 1/v_1 = [κ_1'/p_1'', q_1'/p_1'', 1] = (κ_1'/p_1'')x_1 + (q_1'/p_1'')y_1 + z_1 with integers x_1, y_1, z_1.
- Write (κ_k'/p_k'')x_1 + (q_k'/p_k'')y_1 = v_{k,1}/v_k in lowest terms for k ≥ 2.
- Multiply the three congruences by x_1, y_1, z_1 and add. This gives e_1'/v_1 + e_2'v_{2,1}/v_2 + ... ≡ 0.

(B) Middle block: general elimination of x_1 from the system a·x ≡ 0, b·x ≡ 0, x_i ≡ 0 (mod 1), a_i, b_i rational.
- 1/c_1 = [a_1, b_1, 1] = a_1u_1 + b_1v_1 + w_1, with c_1 a positive integer and [u_1, v_1, w_1] = 1.
- Put a_k u_1 + b_k v_1 = c_{k,1}/c_k.
- Combining with u_1, v_1, w_1 gives x_1/c_1 + Σ_{k≥2} c_{k,1}x_k/c_k ≡ 0.
- c_1a_1 and c_1b_1 are integers. So one may multiply this congruence by c_1a_1, c_1b_1, c_1 and subtract it from the three original congruences.
- This eliminates x_1 and leaves three congruences in x_2, ..., x_n:
  - Σ(a_k − c_1a_1c_{k,1}/c_k)x_k ≡ 0,
  - Σ(b_k − c_1b_1c_{k,1}/c_k)x_k ≡ 0,
  - −Σ c_1c_{k,1}x_k/c_k ≡ 0.
  The last one is exactly the solvability condition for an integer x_1 (my remark).
- Coefficient identities, with (r,s) = a_r b_s − b_r a_s:
  - a_2 − c_1a_1c_{2,1}/c_2 = c_1{a_2(a_1u_1+b_1v_1+w_1) − a_1(a_2u_1+b_2v_1)} = c_1{a_2w_1 − (1,2)v_1},
  - b_2 − c_1b_1c_{2,1}/c_2 = c_1{b_2w_1 + (1,2)u_1},
  - −c_1c_{2,1}/c_2 = c_1{−a_2u_1 − b_2v_1}.
- Together with the coefficient 1 coming from x_2 ≡ 0, the gcd of the four coefficients of x_2 is c_1·[a_2w_1 − (1,2)v_1, b_2w_1 + (1,2)u_1, a_2u_1 + b_2v_1, 1/c_1].
- Dedekind reduces this bracket. First he subtracts a_2 resp. b_2 times the fourth entry, getting [−(1,2)v_1 − a_2(a_1u_1+b_1v_1), (1,2)u_1 − b_2(a_1u_1+b_1v_1), X, 1/c_1] with X = a_2u_1 + b_2v_1. Expanded, these first two entries equal −a_1X and −b_1X (my computation).
- He then drops them and writes [X, 1/c_1] = [c_{2,1}/c_2, 1/c_1].
- Conclusion stated: [c_1c_{2,1}/c_2, 1] is the gcd of the four coefficients of x_2. As shown under errors, this reduction is invalid.

(C) Bottom block (continued on the next page): two unknowns u, v, with the n+2 congruences a_r u + b_r v ≡ 0, u ≡ 0, v ≡ 0.
- Define the modules:
  - 𝔄 = Σ[a_r] + [1],
  - 𝔅 = Σ[b_r] + [1],
  - ℭ = Σ[(r,s)] + Σ[a_r] + Σ[b_r] + [1].
  ℭ is the gcd of all 2×2 minors of the matrix with rows (a_r, b_r), (1,0), (0,1).
- Inclusions: 𝔄, 𝔅 ⊆ ℭ ⊆ 𝔄𝔅. Hence 𝔄 = aℭ, 𝔅 = bℭ, ℭ = c𝔄𝔅 with positive integers a, b, c.
- So ℭ = c·ab·ℭ², giving ℭ = 1/(abc), 𝔄 = 1/(bc), 𝔅 = 1/(ac).
- Choose integers a', a_r' with 1/(bc) = a' + Σ a_r a_r'. Then b'' defined by b''/(ac) = Σ b_r a_r' is an integer, since the sum lies in 𝔅.
- Combining the congruences with a_r', a' gives u/(bc) + b''v/(ac) ≡ 0.
- Since bca_r is an integer, subtracting a_r bc times this congruence gives (a_r u + b_r v) − a_r bc(u/(bc) + b''v/(ac)) = (b_r − a_r bb''/a)v ≡ 0.
- Likewise u − bc(...) = −(bb''/a)v ≡ 0.
- Identity: b_r − a_r bb''/a = bc{a'b_r + b_r Σ a_s a_s'} − bca_r Σ b_s a_s' = bc{a'b_r + Σ(b_r a_s − a_r b_s)a_s'}. This lies in (1/a)Z because bcb_r ∈ (b/a)Z and bc(r,s) ∈ (1/a)Z. Also bb''/a ≡ 0 (mod 1/a).
- Two further identities:
  - (b_r − a_r bb''/a)bca_s − (b_s − a_s bb''/a)bca_r = bc(b_r a_s − a_r b_s),
  - bcb_r = bc(b_r − a_r bb''/a) + bca_r·bb''/a.
  These are used on the next page to show that the gcd 𝔇 of the new coefficients is exactly 1/a.
- Side computation: Σ(b_r − a_r bb''/a)a_r' = b''/(ac) − (1/(bc) − a')bb''/a = a'bb''/a.
- Right column: multiplying by ac gives ab_r − bb''a_r ≡ 0 (mod 1), and acb_r ≡ bca_r·b'' (mod c). The analogue for the entry 1 of 𝔅 is ac·1 ≡ 0·b'' (mod c).
- Hence any common divisor of b'' and c divides every acb_r and ac·1. These generate ac𝔅 = Z, so the divisor divides 1. Thus [b'', c] = 1, and a''b'' + cc'' = 1 for some integers a'', c''.
- Then acb_r a'' ≡ bca_r b''a'' = bca_r(1 − cc'') ≡ bca_r (mod c), i.e. bca_r ≡ a''bca_r b''.
- Also a''(b_r − a_r bb''/a) = a''b_r − a_r b(1 − cc'')/a = a''b_r − ba_r/a + bcc''a_r/a. Rearranged: ba_r/a ≡ bca_r c''/a + a''b_r modulo the new coefficient module (the 'mod ×' at the top right). After multiplying by ac: bca_r ≡ (bca_r)cc'' + a''(acb_r).
- Purpose (completed on the next page): an explicit basis p = u/(bc) + b''v/(ac), q = v/a of the solution lattice. The general solution is v = aq, u = b(cp − b''q), so the solution lattice has index abc = 1/ℭ in Z².
errors: Block (B), reduction of the gcd [a_2w_1 − (1,2)v_1, b_2w_1 + (1,2)u_1, a_2u_1 + b_2v_1, 1/c_1]: subtracting a_2 (resp. b_2) times the entry 1/c_1 is not a legitimate gcd operation, because a_2, b_2 are rational, not integer.
The next step [a_1X, −b_1X, X, 1/c_1] = [X, 1/c_1] is also unjustified: the module contains X/c_1 = u_1(a_1X) + v_1(b_1X) + w_1X, which need not lie in ZX + Z/c_1.

The concluding claim that [c_1c_{2,1}/c_2, 1] is the gcd of the coefficients of x_2 is false in general. Counterexample: a_1 = b_1 = 0, c_1 = 1, u_1 = v_1 = 0, w_1 = 1, a_2 = 1/2, b_2 = 1/3. The true gcd is [1/2, 1/3, 1] = 1/6, but the claim gives [0, 1] = 1. The claim even depends on the arbitrary choice of u_1, v_1.
The fresh start with two unknowns and determinantal modules 𝔄, 𝔅, ℭ right after this may reflect that the first approach was abandoned; this is conjecture.
All identities in blocks (A) and (C) and in the right-hand columns check out.

results.what: Elimination of one unknown from linear congruences mod 1 with rational coefficients via a Bezout combination of the gcd [a_1, b_1, 1]
results.modern_name: Gaussian/Hermite-type elimination over Z for systems in Q/Z (lattice of integer solutions)

results.what: For a two-column system: gcd modules 𝔄, 𝔅, ℭ of entries and 2×2 minors, with ℭ = 1/(abc), 𝔄 = 1/(bc), 𝔅 = 1/(ac), and an explicit basis of the solution lattice of index abc
results.modern_name: Determinantal divisors / Smith normal form for a 2-column matrix; index of the solution lattice equals the reciprocal of the gcd of maximal minors

results.what: Proof that [b'', c] = 1 via acb_r ≡ bca_r b'' (mod c)

deep.surprise_reason: Working notes on lattices of integer solutions of linear congruences mod 1 (elementary-divisor material known from Smith and Frobenius), in Dedekind's module/gcd language. Characteristic of him but not new, and one general claim on the page is actually wrong.

'cab_r − cba_r·b'' ≡ 0 (a)' should be read modulo c; '(a_r)' / '(a)' is a misreading.
'cb.1.b'' ≡ 0 (c)' is probably 'ca·1 − cb·0·b'' ≡ 0 (mod c)' (the analogue for the entry 1), matching 'ac.1 ≡ 0·b''' in the lower box.
In the 1/v_1 block, the struck '+z_1' (rendered A in the image) is crossed out in the second line, so that line reads (κ_2'/p_2'')x_1 + (q_2'/p_2'')y_1 = v_{2,1}/v_2.
